findings.rule: contracts §UI Description — "Range wider than the viewport | The grid scrolls horizontally inside `.time-off-calendar-scroll`; the member column stays pinned"
findings.claim: the horizontal scroll REQ-03-018 makes unconditional is a scroll the member column does not survive: `.time-off-calendar-grid` carries `overflow: hidden`, so it — not the container that actually scrolls — is the scrollport the sticky member cell is positioned against, and the names scroll away with the days

witness.detail: An admin opens /org/{orgId}/time-off/calendar at a 1280x900 viewport, chooses the Range window and picks a 92-day span — the state this spec exists for. The row template is `var(--name-col) repeat(92, minmax(var(--day-col-min), 1fr))` = 264px + 92*32px = 3208px, and `.time-off-calendar-grid` now takes that width at every viewport through the `min-width: max-content` moved out of `@media (max-width: 1199px)` (globals.css:986). `.time-off-calendar-scroll` (globals.css:973-975, `overflow-x: auto`) therefore scrolls. But `.time-off-calendar-grid` sits between the scrolling container and the sticky cell and carries `overflow: hidden` (globals.css:981), which makes it a scroll container in its own right; `.time-off-calendar-who` is `position: sticky; left: 0` (globals.css:1007-1016) and a sticky box is constrained by its NEAREST scroll-container ancestor, whose scroll offset here is permanently 0 because its width equals its content width. Scrolling the container 400px to the right therefore carries every `calendar-member-row-{id}` name cell off the left edge, and the reader is left with 92 unlabelled day columns. The file states the opposite invariant three lines above the sticky rule — globals.css:1004-1006, "The names survive a horizontal scroll — the whole reason the grid scrolls rather than the page" — so the code and the contracts agree on the intent and the cascade defeats both. Under the previous CSS the same ancestor pair existed but the scroll was reachable only below 1200px, where 30 `minmax(0, 1fr)` day columns rarely exceeded the page; this change makes the state routine and central. TC-03-E2E-13 asserts scrollWidth > clientWidth and the column floor, and asserts nothing about the member column's position after a scroll, so no case in the change catches it.
witness.source: specs/time-off/03-calendar-range-and-scope.contracts.md — §UI Description, row "Range wider than the viewport"

findings.suggestedFix: Take the clipping off the sticky element's ancestor chain — move `overflow: hidden` and the `border-radius` onto `.time-off-calendar-scroll` (which is the box that scrolls), leaving `.time-off-calendar-grid` with `overflow: visible` — and extend TC-03-E2E-13 with a read of a `calendar-member-row-{id}` name cell's x after scrolling the container right.

findings.rule: handoff T1 — "The screen and the picker both read this; neither restates the arithmetic"

witness.detail: `grep -rn 'timeOffCalendarLatestEnd' --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx apps packages e2e | grep -v node_modules` returns packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts:267 (the definition), packages/validation/dist/time-off-calendar.d.ts:134 and packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.test.ts:9,291,293,297 — nothing else. CalendarScreen.tsx:440 passes `maxSpanDays={TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MAX_RANGE_DAYS}` and DateRangePicker.tsx:145 computes `addDays(pending, maxSpanDays - 1)` through its own local helper (DateRangePicker.tsx:52-57). The two ends cannot drift on the bound itself, because both derive from the one exported constant; what does not exist is the single definition of the `- 1` the plan named. Checked and accepted as the reason it cannot be shared: `packages/ds` does not depend on `@devscribed/validation` (DateRangePicker.tsx:41-44).

findings.suggestedFix: Either delete the export, or keep it and say in its doc comment that it ships for the tests and that the DS restates the arithmetic because it may not import validation.

findings.rule: contracts §Validation Rules — "The client re-runs rules 1–4 before spending a request"
findings.claim: the screen re-runs none of Validation Rules 1–4, and REQ-03-009's bound is forward-only, so a reader can now build an over-92-day span from the control and spend the request on it

witness.detail: Statement one — contracts.md §Validation Rules, closing paragraph: "The client re-runs rules 1–4 before spending a request; the server re-validates all seven". Statement two — contracts.md §Edge Cases row 7: "A custom range of 93 days, submitted by a client that ignores REQ-03-009 | `422` `rangeTooWide`", which reads as the answer for a NON-compliant client. The code satisfies neither reading: `load` (CalendarScreen.tsx:229-276) never calls `validateTimeOffCalendarRange`, and DateRangePicker.tsx:145 excludes only dates AFTER the armed start, so arming 2026-09-01, paging back and clicking 2026-01-01 commits `[2026-01-01, 2026-09-01]` through commit()'s sort (DateRangePicker.tsx:155-158) — a 244-day span, spent, and answered 422 rangeTooWide. The outcome the reader sees is a message this bundle tabulates, so nothing is broken; what is undecided is whether the compliant client owes a pre-check. REQ-03-009's own heading says "the invalid span is unreachable" while its body and the §UI Description row bound only days after the start, and a reviewer does not settle that.

findings.suggestedFix: Decide it in the document: either the screen owes a span check before the fetch (and the backwards pick is refused client-side), or Edge case 7 is the whole rule and the "client re-runs rules 1–4" sentence does not describe this screen.

findings.rule: reviewer — a fixture whose doc comment claims a safety it does not have
findings.claim: the default `prefix` makes a second call inside one test collide on the unique email column, which is the opposite of what the doc comment promises

witness.detail: `prefix` defaults to `'seeded'` (line 42) and each email is `${prefix}-${index}@seed.test` (line 47) — namespaced by position only, not by organization or by call. A test that seeds an over-cap organization twice, which is exactly what Edge case 1's People-scope mirror would need, throws a Prisma unique-constraint error on `seeded-0@seed.test` on the second call instead of seeding. The doc comment at lines 30-32 states "two calls inside one test do not collide on the unique email column", which holds only if the caller remembers a distinct prefix and the comment does not say so. Nothing fails today: the one call site is apps/api/test/time-off-calendar.spec.ts:1300.

findings.suggestedFix: Fold a per-call token into the email — a module counter or `randomUUID().slice(0, 8)` — so the default is safe, or narrow the comment to say the prefix is the caller's job.
